# Pesher Nahum Column 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Nahum Column 4 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 4:1 — "hashlikhti" — "cast" vs. "fling"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I will-cast filth upon-you" | Standard literal |
| LOGOS | "I will cast filth upon you" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "I will fling filth at you" | More visceral verb |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "cast" (EMET/LOGOS). Hashlikhti (Hiphil of shalakh) is standardly rendered "cast" in prophetic contexts; "fling" is colloquial.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:1 — "re'i" — "gazing-stock" vs. "on display for all to see"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "set-you as-a-gazing-stock" | Preserves re'i as technical term |
| LOGOS | "set you as a gazing-stock" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "put you on display for all to see" | Explanatory paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "gazing-stock" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew re'i means "a spectacle/object of gazing." PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the single-word force.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:3 — "ra'ot" — "evil deeds" vs. "wicked deeds"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "evil deeds" | ra'ot as "evil" |
| LOGOS | "evil deeds" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "wicked deeds" | Synonymous variant |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "evil deeds" (EMET/LOGOS). Ra'ot derives from ra' ("evil/bad"); "wicked" (resha') is a different Hebrew root with different connotations.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:4 — "yakkiru" — "discern" vs. "recognize"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "many will-discern their sin" | nakhar Hiphil as "discern" |
| LOGOS | "many will discern their sin" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "many will recognize their sin" | More accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "discern" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hiphil of nakhar implies active perception and judgment, well captured by "discern."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:4 — "yisne'um" — "hate them" vs. "despise them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-hate-them" | Literal sane' |
| LOGOS | "will hate them" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "despise them" | Slightly different nuance |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "hate" (EMET/LOGOS). Sane' means "hate," not "despise" (bazah). The distinction matters.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:5 — "ga'on 'ashmatam" — "guilty arrogance" vs. "shameful pride"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their guilty arrogance" | ga'on + 'ashmah |
| LOGOS | "their guilty arrogance" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their shameful pride" | Different nuance |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "guilty arrogance" (EMET/LOGOS). 'Ashmah is "guilt" not "shame" (bushah); ga'on is "arrogance/pride" — both are accurately rendered.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:6 — "petayey Ephraim" — "simple ones" vs. "gullible followers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the simple-ones of-Ephraim" | Literal petayim |
| LOGOS | "the simple ones of Ephraim" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "the gullible followers of Ephraim" | Interpretive; adds "followers" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the simple ones of Ephraim." Petayim means "simple/naive"; "gullible" is pejorative beyond the Hebrew, and "followers" is an addition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:7 — "mat'eyhem" — "those who led them astray" vs. "their misleaders"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those-who-led-them-astray" | Hiphil participle expanded |
| LOGOS | "those who led them astray" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "their misleaders" | Condensed noun form |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "those who led them astray." The participial form is more accurate than PNEUMA's noun condensation, and avoids EMET's excessive hyphenation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:9 — "nashammah" — "devastated" vs. "lies in ruins"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Nineveh is-devastated" | Niphal of shamam |
| LOGOS | "Nineveh is devastated" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Nineveh lies in ruins" | More concrete image |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "is devastated" (EMET/LOGOS). Nashammah (Niphal perfect of shamam) means "is laid waste/devastated." "Lies in ruins" shifts from the verbal action to a static description.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:9 — "yanud" — "grieve" vs. "mourn"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "who will-grieve for-her" | nud as "grieve" |
| LOGOS | "who will grieve for her" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "who will mourn for her" | Standard synonym |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "grieve" (EMET/LOGOS). Nud specifically means "to shake the head in sympathy/grief" — "grieve" captures this better than "mourn" (which would be 'aval or saphad).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:11 — "'edah" — "congregation" vs. "followers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their congregation" | Consistent 'edah rendering |
| LOGOS | "their congregation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their followers" | Interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "congregation" (EMET/LOGOS), consistent with all prior rulings on 'edah.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:13 — "'atsah" — "council" vs. "schemes"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their council" | 'atsah as "council/counsel" |
| LOGOS | "their council" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their schemes" | Pejorative interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "council" (EMET/LOGOS). 'Atsah means "counsel/council"; "schemes" imports negative judgment beyond the word itself.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:14 — "No-Amon" — preserved vs. "Thebes"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "No-Amon" | Preserves Hebrew form |
| LOGOS | "No-Amon" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Thebes" | Modern identification for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "No-Amon" (EMET/LOGOS). The pesher quotes the biblical text of Nahum, which uses the Hebrew name No-Amon. Substituting the Greek name Thebes departs from the source text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:16 — "chel" — "rampart" vs. "defense"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "whose rampart was the sea" | chel as "rampart" |
| LOGOS | "whose rampart was the sea" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "with the river as her defense" | "defense" more general; adds "river" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "rampart" (EMET/LOGOS). Chel is a specific fortification term meaning "rampart/wall." PNEUMA's "defense" is too general, and substituting "river" for "sea" departs from the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 4:** 14
